title: Left derived values invert the multiplicative system
statement: In Situation 05S8 [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization], let $s:X\to Y$ be a morphism in $S$. Then $LF$ is defined at $X$ if and only if it is defined at $Y$, and in this case the map $LF(s):LF(X)\to LF(Y)$ between values [lem-pur-derived-functor-morphisms-05sa] is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Write J_X=S/X and J_Y=S/Y for the cofiltered denominator categories of Definition 05S9. Since s lies in S, MS1 gives a functor c:J_X→J_Y, (u:X'→X) ↦ (s∘u:X'→Y), and the pro-diagram of J_Y composed with c is literally the pro-diagram (u:X'→X) ↦ F(X') of J_X. The functor c is initial: for every denominator t:Z→Y, the second MS2 clause applied to t∈S and s gives a denominator u:W→X and v:W→Z with t∘v=s∘u, i.e. a morphism c(u)→t in J_Y; and given two morphisms c(u)→t, c(u')→t, pass to a common object u'' of the cofiltered J_X mapping to u and u', so that one gets two maps a,b:W''→Z with t∘a=t∘b, and the second MS3 clause (t∈S with source Z) gives a denominator r with a∘r=b∘r, which (composed into J_X) connects the two morphisms. By Stacks Categories Lemma 0A1T (restriction along an initial functor of cofiltered categories), the pro-diagram of J_X is essentially constant exactly when that of J_Y is. Therefore LF is defined at X if and only if it is defined at Y.

proof.text: Assume both values exist. Lemma 05SA(2) gives LF(s):LF(X)→LF(Y). Use the reverse MS2 comparison: for each denominator s':Y'→Y choose a denominator t':X'→X and a map t:X'→Y' with s∘t'=s'∘t. Applying F(t) and the cone maps defines a morphism LF(Y)→LF(X); MS3 makes it independent of the chosen square. After a further common denominator, MS3 also makes each composite equal to the corresponding identity comparison. The uniqueness clause of 05SA(2) then identifies the composites with id_{LF(X)} and id_{LF(Y)}, so LF(s) is an isomorphism.
